Name: Marsha Tyson
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

In physics, we use a lot of multi-modal text. We use charts, graphs, and equations. We use pictures and written text. I think starting with a picture or info graphic is a great way to start with they say/I say. It eases students into the process and they and gain confidence.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I believe it is essential to incorporate partner talk into sensemaking of text. Particularly if it is a more difficult text or has multiple perspectives to consider. I think this could also be modified to incorporate a whiteboard. Students complete They Say/I say individually and then share as a larger group where they chart their thoughts for everyone to see. Then you could gallery walk all of the whiteboard and see the variations in responses.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I don’t have any needs at this point. The course is providing many ways to reflect and I loved seeing some of the example slides in this module I could copy and use.
